questions.question_english: If an earthquake occurs while students are outdoors on the school playground, what is the recommended safety action?
options_english: Run back inside the school building for shelter.
Move away from buildings, trees, streetlights, and utility wires, and drop to the ground.
Stand as close as possible to the exterior structural wall of the building to avoid exposure to direct sunlight
Scatter and run randomly across the field.
questions.explanation_english: Move away from buildings, trees, streetlights, and utility wires, and drop to the ground. When outdoors during seismic activity, individuals must move away from exterior building walls, overhead electric lines, tall trees, and light poles. Remaining in open sports grounds away from falling structures reduces impact risks from collapsing architectural elements or falling power cables. Dropping to the ground maintains balance and prevents fall injuries caused by ground displacement.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है: भवनों, पेड़ों, स्ट्रीट लाइटों और बिजली के तारों से दूर जाकर जमीन पर झुकना। इस उपाय से पहचाने गए जोखिमों को कम करने, आपात स्थिति के लिए तैयारी बढ़ाने और विद्यार्थियों तथा कर्मचारियों की सुरक्षित निकासी/सुरक्षा में मदद मिलती है।

questions.explanation_english: Identifying and mitigating traffic and physical hazards on the paths students use to commute to and from school Safe Route to School initiatives focus on identifying and eliminating traffic hazards, physical dangers, and infrastructure gaps along student commuting routes. questions.question_english: During a surprise inspection, the Fire Safety Officer finds that the school’s emergency exit route is partially blocked by old, discarded furniture. As the Principal, what is the most appropriate compliance action?
options_english: Wait for the upcoming annual institutional auction of obsolete goods before moving or clearing out the stacked furniture.
Immediately order the removal of the furniture to ensure the escape route is 100% unobstructed.
Argue that the main gate is sufficient and leave the obstruction in place

questions.explanation_english: Immediately order the removal of the furniture to ensure the escape route is 100% unobstructed. Obstructions in designated emergency exit routes pose immediate, life-threatening risks during emergency evacuations. Ordering immediate removal of stored items or obsolete furniture restores required corridor widths and guarantees unobstructed escape pathways. Maintaining clear evacuation routes at all times is a strict legal mandate essential for preventing crush hazards, delays, or entrapment during sudden structural emergencies.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है: निकासी मार्ग को पूरी तरह अवरोध-मुक्त करने के लिए तुरंत फर्नीचर हटाना। इस उपाय से पहचाने गए जोखिमों को कम करने, आपात स्थिति के लिए तैयारी बढ़ाने और विद्यार्थियों तथा कर्मचारियों की सुरक्षित निकासी/सुरक्षा में मदद मिलती है।

questions.explanation_english: Improperly secured heavy almirahs and bookshelves in the library Non-structural hazards refer to internal items, fixtures, or furnishings that are not part of a building’s load-bearing architecture but pose significant risks during emergencies. Securing such interior items through proper anchorage is a critical non-structural mitigation practice in school disaster management.

The biometric login required to access school computers

questions.question_english: What is the correct protocol for evacuation during an earthquake drill?
options_english: Evacuate immediately while the ground is still violently shaking.
Remain completely inside the classroom building for at least two full hours after the initial earthquake shaking stops
Wait until the shaking stops entirely, then evacuate in an orderly manner to the open assembly area.

questions.explanation_english: Wait until the shaking stops entirely, then evacuate in an orderly manner to the open assembly area. Immediate structural evacuation during active seismic shaking is dangerous due to falling debris, destabilized stairways, and loss of footing. Occupants must shelter under sturdy furniture during active tremors and wait until ground motion ceases completely. Systematic post- shake evacuation along pre-mapped safe routes prevents trip injuries and panic while moving populations to open assembly grounds.
